title: Redwood Optimize walkthrough - batching & KV cache (Mistral Payments)
summary: Redwood AE+SE ran an Optimize walkthrough focused on batching and KV/prefix caching for Mistral Payments' conversational payments use case. Discussed tradeoffs (latency vs cost), quantization and model variants, security requirements (SOC 2, KMS, VPC), and proposed a 4-week POC with benchmark plan. Action items include sending pricing, security docs, and a benchmark script.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-14 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Camille Park (Redwood SE), Mike Alvarez (CTO - Mistral), Sara Kim (Eng Mgr), Liam O'Neill (Infra), Aisha Banerjee (Security), Diego Torres (Product)

Summary (auto): quick Optimize walkthrough focused on batching and KV/prefix caching. Covered how prefix caching reduces per-token compute for repetitive prompts, baseline cost model examples, and POC plan + security questions.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh let's do quick intros. I'm Jordan, AE on the Redwood team, and with me is Priya our SE. Camille will jump in on the demo bits. How's everyone doing?
[00:16] Mike: Good, thanks. We're excited — huge opportunity to reduce token costs for our chat flows, especially the 4-step payment auth flow that repeats context.
[00:30] Priya: Awesome. Today we'll focus on Optimize: batching and caching recs, prefix vs KV cache, and give you a cost model example with numbers you can use for the POC. We'll also touch on security / VPC / KMS stuff.
[00:45] Sara: Quick ask — we'd like to understand latency impact. We have a 200ms p50 target for auth path.
[00:52] Priya: Totally, we'll call out tradeoffs — batching helps throughput and unit cost but can increase tail latency, whereas prefix/KV cache can drop per-token compute significantly for repeated prefixes with minimal latency impact if tuned.
[01:10] Camille: I'll start a short demo of how cache hits look in the Console and how the cost calc updates live. bear with transcription hiccups, my mic's a bit low.
[01:28] [Screenshare starts] Camille: here in Console -> Optimize -> Caching tab. You can see our prefix cache config and the KV cache table. For this example we have an auth prefix that's ~120 tokens and a variable user prompt of ~30 tokens. If the prefix is cached we only decode the variable tokens on each request.
[02:05] Liam: so are you storing user-specific keys in the KV cache or is it shared?
[02:12] Priya: Good q. Typically keys are per-session id, we recommend salted session keys for security; the cache store can be isolated per-customer on Dedicated or via VPC private deploys. For hosted we do tenant isolation and TTLs.
[02:34] Diego: Do you have rough numbers — like percent cost reduction for our flows?
[02:41] Priya: In our experience for payment flows with long stable prefixes you can see 40-65% token compute reduction with prefix/KV cache. Example: baseline no-cache cost $0.085 per request (gen cost), with prefix cached it's $0.034 per request on same model and sequence lengths — big win. Those are ballpark, we'll run benchmarks on your sample traffic to tune.
[03:18] Mike: That's promising. What about batching? Our peak concurrent is ~180 rps and p50 target 200ms.
[03:27] Priya: Batching improves GPU throughput and lowers cost per token by filling micro-batches — but if you batch too long you add queuing latency. We recommend adaptive batching: target a short batching window (5-10ms) with a max batch size aligned to the model footprint. For 180 rps, with continuous batching we can often keep p50 within 150-230ms depending on model and quantization.
[03:58] Jordan: And we can route by policy — hot path auth -> low-latency pool, lower-cost pool for async workloads. That lets you keep SLAs for auth.
[04:10] Aisha: Security question: do cached prefixes ever leave the customer's VPC? How is encryption handled?
[04:18] Priya: For Private deployments, all cache data remains in your VPC. For Dedicated we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for at-rest encryption and TLS in transit. We also emit audit logs for cache reads/writes as part of the message audit stream.
[04:38] Aisha: And SOC 2 artifacts?
[04:41] Jordan: We'll share the SOC 2 pack and our security whitepaper after this call — action item noted.
[04:50] [05:00] Camille: demo — here's a simulated traffic run. Notice cache hit ratio on left panel — after warmup it's ~78% for the auth prefix. On the right, cost estimate drops in real time, and you can toggle quantization (8-bit) which further lowers GPU time.
[05:38] Sara: About quantization: do you have quality regressions? We care about correctness for payment instruction parsing.
[05:45] Priya: We do regression tests tied to eval prompts. Quantization to 8-bit (Q8) usually has negligible quality change for our tuned model variants, but we recommend a short eval sweep on your critical prompts. We'll include a regression harness in the repo.
[06:12] Mike: Can you explain prefix vs KV cache — I'm not 100% clear on difference in practice.
[06:18] Priya: Sure — prefix cache stores a fixed token prefix and the corresponding KV (key-value) attention cache so future requests that reuse that prefix can skip re-encoding it. KV cache is the general mechanism; prefix caching is an application of KV caching where you precompute a shared prefix. Think of prefix cache as a named entry in the KV store keyed by prompt template or session.
[06:45] Liam: How often do we need to refresh those caches? If policy text changes monthly that's fine but what about ephemeral data?
[06:52] Priya: TTLs and invalidation policies are configurable. For highly dynamic data we recommend short TTLs or skip caching. For static legal / policy text, set long TTLs and pin the prefix version.
[07:12] Diego: Could caching cause stale responses if prompt text or persona changes?
[07:18] Priya: Only if the prefix itself changes and you don't invalidate. Cache keys should include versioning metadata. We'll share best-practice naming conventions in the POC runbook.
[07:35] [10:00] Camille: switching to cost model spreadsheet — I'll show a sample for Mistral. Baseline assumptions: avg seq len 160 tokens, prefix 120 cached, user tokens 40. Model run cost baseline (no cache) $0.085/request. With prefix cached plus batching & Q8 quant, we estimate $0.018-0.032/request depending on hit rate and batching efficiency.
[10:40] Mike: That delta is huge — what inputs drive it most?
[10:45] Priya: Hit rate, avg prefix length, and batching efficiency. Hit rate is the multiplier — 80% hits means 80% of requests skip the prefix decode. Batching lowers per-token GPU cost but can add ms. We gave a simple sensitivity table in the sheet to play with numbers.
[11:10] Sara: For our 200ms p50 requirement, will the Q8 + caching + batching combo meet it?
[11:16] Priya: Likely yes on p50; we need to measure p95. We'll run a POC that simulates your traffic and measure p50/p95 under target batching windows. If p95 is high we can route auth to a low-latency pool (dedicated GPUs or smaller batch windows).
[11:38] Aisha: On the compliance front, will Redwood's logging include enough for us to satisfy auditors? We need request-level logging and redaction controls.
[11:46] Jordan: We provide request-level traces in Console with PII redaction options and retention policies. For Private deployments, you control retention. We'll send examples.
[12:00] [15:00] Priya: quick note on model variants — you can pick a slightly smaller/quantized variant for auth if you need latency. We also support fallback policies: if cheap pool overloaded, route to a higher-latency SLO-preserving route.
[15:25] Diego: Any impact to developer experience? How do we integrate with our existing API?
[15:30] Camille: No SDK changes for caching — you annotate the prompt template and call the caching endpoint; we have a small SDK helper. We'll include code snippets in the runbook.
[16:02] Mike: Let's talk acceptance criteria for the POC — what would success look like?
[16:08] Jordan: Good question. Proposed success: (1) p50 <= 220ms for auth path under production-like load, (2) cost per auth request reduced at least 40% vs baseline, (3) no regression on 10 critical end-to-end prompts. If we hit those, we move to pilot and Dedicated sizing.
[16:36] Sara: Sounds fair. Timeline?
[16:40] Jordan: We suggested a 4-week POC: week 0 onboarding/traffic ingest; week 1 warmup + baseline; week 2 tuning (cache + batching); week 3 measurement and handoff. Aim to start wk of 10/26.
[17:00] Priya: I'll outline the benchmark script now — it simulates your traffic, warms cache, runs p50/p95 sweeps, and captures cost. We use both synthetic and replayed anonymized traffic.
[17:25] Liam: Re: data — we can export an anonymized stream. Security will want to review before sharing.
[17:30] Aisha: Yep, we'll validate. On KMS, we need to know if Redwood supports external HSMs for key custody.
[17:36] Priya: Yes for Private we support customer-managed KMS + HSM integrations; for Dedicated we have KMS integration options. We'll add the HSM FAQ to the security pack.
[17:50] [25:00] Camille: demo wrap — showing Console's cost forecast and how to toggle hit rates to see impact. If you bump hit rate from 50% to 80% you see unit cost drop ~2.4x in the model.
[25:40] Diego: Any gotchas with multi-tenant Dedicated pools?
[25:45] Jordan: Dedicated means reserved capacity for you, but you can still choose host-managed or customer-managed network enclaves. We can size pools to avoid noisy neighbor issues.
[26:05] Sara: What about SDK latency — do we need client-side batching or is it server-side only?
[26:12] Priya: Server-side continuous batching is default, we also support application-level micro-batching if you want more control. Often server-side is enough.
[26:30] Mike: Competitive question — we've been talking to Anthropic and AWS — what's Redwood's angle?
[26:36] Jordan: We're focused on production economics and observability — tuneable batching, prefix/KV caching, and transparent cost models. We give routing and rollback tools to keep apps up. We'll share a comparative note.
[26:55] Aisha: Ok, last security clarifications — audit log retention, SSO/SAML integration, and certs.
[27:02] Jordan: All supported; we'll add the specific retention options and SAML metadata to the security packet.
[27:18] [35:00] Priya: action items recap: Jordan send pricing & sample cost model, Priya send benchmark scripts + runbook, Camille will attach Console screenshots and the sample spreadsheet, customer to provide anonymized traffic and security requirements.
[35:40] Diego: Thanks, that helps. We'll try to get traffic by next Tue.
[36:05] Jordan: Great — we'll follow up with calendar invite for a POC kickoff and include the security docs.
[36:20] Sara: Quick note — we need a signed NDA before we share some logs. Is there a standard one?
[36:26] Jordan: Yes, we have a standard mutual NDA, I'll send it with the pricing email.
[36:40] [45:00] Mike: Any concerns on our side? I think we need to see the p95 numbers.
[45:06] Priya: Agreed. We'll focus on getting p95 down in the run. If needed, we recommend a dedicated low-latency pool for the auth route.
[45:28] Jordan: ok final recap: POC kickoff wk of 10/26; Jordan send pricing + NDA + security pack; Priya share benchmark + runbook; Mistral to provide traffic + identify 10 critical prompts.
[45:50] Aisha: We'll review the security pack and confirm KMS/HSM requirements.
[46:05] Diego: I'll coordinate traffic export with Liam.
[46:15] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up.
[52:00] End call
